authorities.proposition: The courts of appeals have jurisdiction over final decisions of the district courts, subject to statutory exceptions.
Unless another provision of section 2107 applies, a civil notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days after entry of the judgment, order, or decree.

A judgment ordinarily must be set out in a separate document. When a separate document is required, entry occurs upon docket entry and the earlier of a compliant separate document or 150 days after docket entry.
When an appeal is dismissed, costs are taxed against the appellant unless the parties agree otherwise or the court orders otherwise.

authorities.citation: Kinsale Insurance Co. v. JDBC Holdings, Inc., 31 F.4th 870 (4th Cir. 2022)
authorities.locator: Majority Parts I–II, official PDF pages 3–11; concurrence follows
authorities.proposition: Rule 54(b) requires ultimate disposition of an individual claim and a case-specific no-just-reason determination. Certification is tilted against fragmentation and considers claim relationship, possible mootness, repeat appellate review, setoff, and other equities; stated findings support abuse-of-discretion review.

authorities.citation: McPherson v. Patton, No. 23-1938 (4th Cir. Oct. 15, 2024) (unpublished)
authorities.proposition: In a nonprecedential disposition, a grant of a Rule 54(b) motion and partial judgment did not become final when the district court omitted the express no-just-reason determination; the appeal was dismissed and remanded.
The statutory time limit for filing a civil notice of appeal is jurisdictional and courts may not create equitable exceptions to it.

Virginia enforces clear contractual conditions precedent. Contract interpretation is reviewed de novo, and denying a contracting party the benefit of an express prerequisite supports enforcement; the appropriate consequence for noncompliance depends on the contract and case circumstances.
